lawson_creek_finding.method: curl of the official City of New Bern Boat Ramps page (WebFetch returned almost no text). The page is 200 HTML; the facility content is a city-hosted JPEG layout map.
lawson_creek_finding.map_title: Boat Ramps by Status in City of New Bern Parks
lawson_creek_finding.finding: The official map labels four city boat ramps: Glenburnie Ramp, Union Point Ramp, Lawson Creek Ramp 1, and Lawson Creek Ramp 2, each with the legend “Open.” Lawson Creek is therefore treated as two verified public city boat ramps, not as an unconfirmed site. Glenburnie Ramp is added (it was not in the Phase One inventory). The “Open” legend is from a graphic dated May 6, 2025, still posted Nov 22, 2026; it is not a live confirmation. Numeric coordinates, lane counts, and parking counts are not published on the graphic. Directions use official park addresses from the city’s parks list: Lawson Creek Park, 1309 Country Club Road; Glenburnie Park, 340 Glenburnie Drive; Union Point Park, 210 East Front Street.

phase_one_overlap.explanation: Phase One’s 45 + 5 + 9 = 59 did not sum to 53 because the buckets were not mutually exclusive. Newport (verified, shallow-canal restriction) was counted in both “verified public trailered” (45) and “not a general gas-motorboat launch” (9). The 9 also included all 5 needs-review sites plus three verified hard-restriction sites (South 10th Street, 16 feet or less; Beaverdam, non-gas only; B.W. Wells, campers only). The mutually exclusive repair is listing_class general / limited / needs_review. Newport and Moonlight Drive (3 trailer spaces) stay in general, with a standing caution or limited-parking note. Phase Two official-page check then replaced the single Lawson Creek needs-review record with two verified Lawson Creek ramps and added Glenburnie Ramp (53 − 1 + 3 = 55).

filter_rules.default_description: Verified public trailered motorboat launches suitable for general use. Standing cautions (shallow draft) and limited-but-usable parking remain visible in the default list.
optional_filters: Show limited-access launches (listing_class == limited), or the individual flags camper_only, non_gas_only, size_limited, and no_parking.
Show needs-review entries (listing_class == needs_review). Needs-review records stay in a clearly labeled section even when a restriction flag also matches.

fees.summary: No separate boat-launch fee is stated. NC State Parks charges a parking/vehicle entrance fee at Falls Lake, Jordan Lake, and Kerr Lake State Recreation Areas of $10 per motor vehicle per day ($5 with a senior citizen or military member/veteran in the vehicle; $20 per bus). The fee is charged only on weekends and holidays in April, May, and September, and daily from Memorial Day to Labor Day. On other days and months, day-use accesses at the reservoirs have no entrance fee. A Seasonal Parking Pass is $60 per year ($70 beginning with 2026 passes) and covers one vehicle entrance fee per day. Source: NC State Parks Reservation Rates and Activity Fees, checked Nov 22, 2026. This is seasonal fee information, not a real-time status.

hours.summary: Day-use area hours on the official 2026 park pages: Jan, Feb, Nov, Dec 8 a.m.-6 p.m.; Mar, Apr, Sep, Oct 8 a.m.-8 p.m.; May-Aug 8 a.m.-9 p.m. All NC State Parks facilities are closed on Christmas Day. Jordan Lake day-use area gates and most campground gates open and lock promptly at the posted times; no entry or exit is permitted when the gates are closed, except for law enforcement or medical emergencies (Crosswinds and Poplar Point campground gates have 24-hour access). These are scheduled hours, not a live open/closed check. Beaverdam day-use boat ramp (non-gas only) is listed open year-round.
